correctness.rationale: For every admissible positive Leslie pair, the explicit polynomial is verified symbolically as both trace difference and commutator determinant; monodromies share positive determinant, and their Perron roots are ordered by trace. All three single-vital-rate signed-square identities are exact, both rational persistence examples have det(monodromy)<1 with opposite det(I-M) signs, and short-period impossibility follows from cyclic word classes. Included checker was run on actual path and passed.

The two-by-two commutator determinant identity can be specialized to derive the rules and is acknowledged as the algebraic precursor.

originality.rationale: The precise assessed contribution is the exact global Leslie-family sign criterion and three universal single-vital-rate signs, with opposite exact persistence witnesses. The broad phenomenon of order dependence and explicit AABB/ABAB comparison were already established in Mertens et al. (2002) and are excluded from novelty. General periodic projection frameworks and the two-by-two trace identity are predecessors. None of the accessible inspected source material explicitly states the specialized three-part universal sign trichotomy, but unread primary full text leaves real historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: A natural demographic distinction between early-fertility, mature-fertility and maturation-survival seasonal changes yields three opposite universal scheduling rules; two exact admissible populations reverse deterministic viability verdicts. The minimal period-four length is a motivated structural boundary and the polynomial signs delimit applicability beyond a single changing vital rate. This is a narrow population-theory lemma, not a new general statement about temporal order, and has clear conditional planning relevance.
